case_title: Manoharan v. State by Inspector of Police, Variety Hall Police Station, Coimbatore
confession: Yes, recorded before Magistrate u/s.164 CrPC, partially retracted
aggravating_circumstances: Rape of a minor girl, murder of two children, cold-blooded crime, no remorse shown
mitigating_circumstances: Young age, poor family, first-time offender, not the mastermind
high_court_outcome: Set aside conviction u/ss.120-B and 364-A, confirmed conviction u/ss.376, 302, s.302 r/w ss.34 and 201
neutral_facts: The accused, along with a co-accused, abducted a 10-year-old girl and her 7-year-old brother, who were waiting to go to school. The co-accused then picked up the accused from his house. The girl was raped and sodomized, and both children were administered poison mixed in milk. They spat out the substance and only ingested a small portion. Since poisoning did not work, the children were thrown into a nearby canal, causing their death by drowning. The co-accused was shot dead by the police in an encounter. The accused recorded a confession before a magistrate under Section 164 CrPC, which was partially retracted. The prosecution examined forty-nine witnesses, including those who witnessed the abduction, purchase of milk and cow dung powder, and those who saw the children in the custody of the accused. Medical and forensic evidence confirmed drowning and rape, as well as injuries on the accused's body. The trial court convicted the accused of rape and murder, and the High Court confirmed the conviction. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction and confirmed the death sentence.
